_comment: The frozen record this surface is generated from. build-site.mjs reads it and emits index.html; launch-gate.mjs reads the EMITTED index.html and refuses to publish when the artifact and this file disagree. Nothing on the page may state a rung, a status or a scope that is not here.
_shell_revision_comment: The revision of agents/SHELL.md this surface was built against. SHELL.md's own revision block asks for it, and the reason is good: every lane so far has found a defect in that document, and a surface that records which revision it was built against is the only way to know later which pages carry a fix and which predate it. r4 = tier-4 band variant, --fg3 at .55, §8 identifying animation required. NOTE: the revision block was added to SHELL.md while this lane was running; the document read at the start of the run already contained all of r2, r3 and r4, so this surface is r4 in substance as well as in label.
_nav_tier_comment: ampersand-nav/src/amp-nav.js (HEAD d0a6415) records `deliberatic: { place: 3, rung: "spec", spec: "…docs.ampersandboxdesign.com…" }`. Place 3 is "a specification in the ComputeDriven world" — NOT the place-2 layer sentence, and NOT the place-4 attribution variant. SHELL.md §1 says check the tier before you write the band, because that is exactly how gpscoord shipped a membership claim its own nav excluded. Checked 2026-08-16.
question: Can disagreement be preserved and governed rather than averaged away?
surface_rung_covers: the protocol document at docs/spec/README.md, v0.1-draft — no line of Deliberatic has been written and nothing on this domain runs
_rung_witness_comment: Which gate establishes the surface rung. launch-gate.mjs refuses if THAT gate is not approved. GPSCoord's rule — 'any pending gate keeps the surface below live_deployed' — is too blunt: independent_use is pending forever by construction, so under that rule no surface could ever reach a deployed rung.

status.statement: A specification, and this page. The weighted bipolar argumentation framework, the two-phase consensus, the constitution DSL, the Merkle evidence chains and the reputation system are all written down in detail, and none of them have been implemented.
status.source: docs/spec/README.md in this repository, v0.1-draft. Every section number cited on this page was checked to resolve in it on 2026-08-16.
status.limit: This establishes that a document exists and that it addresses the dimensions named below. It does not establish that the semantics converge on any real graph, that the consensus protocol is correct, or that a single line of Deliberatic has ever run. A specification that covers a gap and a system that closes it are different objects.

advance.requires: Code in a repository that implements §2.2 graded semantics and passes a test. The transport bindings in §7 are specified for A2A, MCP and raw HTTP, so an implementation that is not ours would move this further still — that is the only thing that can.

citation.title: Governance Gaps in Agent Interoperability Protocols: What MCP, A2A, and ACP Cannot Express
citation._peer_reviewed_comment: It is a preprint. The page says so in --warn, and the paper's own 'Partial classification involves judgment' limitation is quoted rather than hidden. A source cited only where it flatters is not a source.
citation.scoring: 2 points for Supported, 1 for Partial, 0 for Absent, over six dimensions — 12 possible.

contact._comment: Deliberately not a mailto: — Travis's call, 2026-08-11 — and deliberately not another surface's Formspree endpoint. This page carried no mailto:; its two siblings did, and both are removed in the same commit. Whether the governance trio gets a Formspree endpoint of its own is [TRAVIS].

gates._comment: A gate may not read approved without its evidence, reviewer and date fields, and launch-gate.mjs enforces that.

spec_document_exists.label: The specification this page describes is in the tree and its cited sections resolve
spec_document_exists.description: Every section number printed on this page — 2.1, 2.2, 3.1, 3.2, 3.3, 4.1, 5.1, 5.2, 6.1, 7.1 — was matched against the headings of docs/spec/README.md.
spec_document_exists.evidence: grep -nE '^#{1,3} ' docs/spec/README.md, compared against the section references emitted into index.html; re-checked mechanically by launch-gate.mjs on every run.
spec_document_exists.reviewer: launch-gate.mjs, run against the emitted index.html

source_read_not_summarised.label: The cited preprint was read, not summarised
source_read_not_summarised.description: Every quoted definition is the paper's own wording, taken from the HTML rather than a search result or a PDF summariser. This project has produced a wrong taxonomy twice from summarising passes, in this exact subject area.
source_read_not_summarised.evidence: arxiv.org/html/2606.31498v1, read directly; the paper's own 'Partial classification involves judgment' limitation is quoted on the page.

implementation.label: Any of this has been implemented
implementation.description: There is no code. The rung is spec and stays there until something runs.

deployed_route_check.label: This revision answers on deliberatic.com
deployed_route_check.description: The deployed copy is the previous revision. Nothing here has been read back from the domain it describes.

independent_use.label: Someone who is not us implemented or refuted the specification
independent_use.description: The only rung nobody here can award themselves. An outside implementation of §2.2, or a filed issue showing the semantics do not converge.
